assessmentSettings.feedbackPolicy: Show concise learning feedback after submission; keep full answer keys in the teacher setup file.

requiredUploads: thin-lens-evidence.png — four lens observations plus three verified calculation rows
requiredCopiedValues: Students type short values read from the on-screen tables; the assessment template blocks clipboard actions.

humanReviewTriggers: Student response conflicts with the uploaded evidence image.
Student reports values that fall outside the expected range but the evidence image may support them.
Student gives a partially correct explanation that does not fit the rubric cleanly.
Student uses valid alternative vocabulary or reasoning not covered by the model answer.
Student answer is blank, copied from the prompt, or too vague to verify.
Student cites no data when the prompt requires their own recorded values.

questions.prompt: State the mathematical thin-lens model that connects focal length f, object distance p, and image distance q. Use reciprocal sums from at least two lens trials to explain why the constant belongs to the lens and how it gives the focal length.
questions.gradedOn: Your response is graded on stating the thin-lens relationship, citing reciprocal sums from at least two of your trials, and converting that constant into a focal length.

criteria: Cites at least two sums close to 0.0667 cm^-1.
Explains that the sum remains constant while p and q change because the same lens is used.
Takes the reciprocal to obtain f near 15.0 cm.
Gives the equation and focal length with limited evidence or explanation.
Gives an unrelated model or no data-based reasoning.

commonMisconceptions: Reports the focal length without taking the reciprocal of the sum.
Treats the reciprocal sum as varying between trials.
Cites only one trial, so the constant is not demonstrated.

feedback.fullCredit: Strong work. Your answer uses your own recorded data and connects it to the correct physics idea.
feedback.partialCredit: Revise by adding the specific values you recorded and naming the physics concept that explains them.
feedback.noCredit: Return to your evidence image, identify the values this question asks about, and explain them using the target concept.
feedback.teacherNote: Flag for review if the reasoning is unusual but could be correct, or if the cited values disagree with the uploaded evidence.

questions.prompt: Use operational evidence from all four lens trials to distinguish real and virtual images. Explain what the screen and ray diagram show for L1-L3 compared with L4, and include orientation in your comparison.
questions.gradedOn: Your response is graded on the operational evidence you cite from the screen and the ray diagram, and on whether you compare orientation as well as image type.

criteria: Explains that L1-L3 form sharp, inverted images on a screen, which is direct evidence that the rays converge to real images. Explains that L4 cannot be focused on the screen.
Its outgoing rays diverge and only their backward extensions meet at an upright, enlarged virtual image.
Correctly distinguishes the trials but omits screen evidence, ray behavior, or orientation.
Reverses real and virtual or provides no operational evidence.

commonMisconceptions: Calls the virtual image real because it can be seen through the lens.
Omits that a real image can be caught on a screen.
Reverses the orientation of the real and virtual images.
